title.vi: Part 2 · Mô tả một nơi công cộng bạn thích
title.en: Part 2 · Describe a public place you enjoy
title.ru: Part 2 · Опишите общественное место, которое вам нравится

prompt:
Describe a public place in your town or city that you enjoy visiting.
You should say:
- where it is
- what people do there
- how often you go there
and explain why you enjoy visiting it.

samples.text: I want to talk about a park near my house. It is name Green Park. It is about ten minutes from my house by walk. In the park, people do exercise, they run, and old people do, er, tai chi in the morning. Children play in the playground. I go there maybe two or three time a week, usually in the evening after school. I like it because it is very green and the air is fresh, not like the street. Also it is free so everybody can go. Sometimes I meet my friends there and we, um, sit and talk. I think it is a good place for relax. That's all.

samples.text:
The place I'd like to describe is Green Park, which is a large park about a ten-minute walk from my home. It's quite old, I think it was built more than fifty years ago, and it has a lake in the middle and lots of big trees.

People do many different things there. In the early morning you can see elderly people doing tai chi or dancing to music, and later in the day there are people jogging, families having picnics and children playing on the swings. At weekends there's sometimes a small market selling plants and handmade things.

I go there about three times a week, usually in the evening, to walk or just sit by the lake after studying.

The main reason I enjoy it is that it helps me relax. My street is very noisy and crowded, so walking in the park feels like a break from all that. I also like watching people, because everyone seems happy there. Sometimes I meet my friends and we walk around the lake and chat for an hour or so. I think every city needs places like this.

samples.text:
I'm going to talk about Green Park, which is a fairly large park tucked away behind the main shopping street, just a ten-minute walk from where I live.

What I love about it is how many different groups share the space. At dawn it belongs to the older generation: you'll see dozens of people doing tai chi or ballroom dancing to a little portable speaker. By mid-morning it's mostly parents with toddlers, and in the evening it fills up with joggers, students like me and couples strolling around the lake.

I'd say I go three or four times a week, usually after dinner, when the heat has died down. It's become a bit of a ritual: I do a couple of laps of the lake and then sit on the same bench and watch the sky change colour.

As for why I enjoy it, I think it's mainly because it gives me some breathing space. My neighbourhood is packed with traffic and construction noise, so stepping into the park is like turning the volume down. It's also one of the few places in the city where people of all ages mix without having to spend any money, which I think is quite special.

samples.text:
The place that immediately springs to mind is Green Park, a slightly scruffy but much-loved park squeezed in behind the main shopping street, about ten minutes on foot from my flat.

It's an interesting place to people-watch, because it changes character completely over the course of a day. Early in the morning it's taken over by retirees doing tai chi in perfect unison, or practising ballroom dancing with a crackly speaker propped against a tree. By lunchtime office workers drift in with takeaway boxes, and in the evening it's all joggers, teenagers on skateboards and families feeding the ducks.

I try to go most evenings, so four or five times a week, and I've more or less claimed a bench by the lake as my own.

Why do I like it so much? Partly it's simply a refuge. I live above a busy road, and the park is the one spot nearby where I can actually hear birds instead of horns. But I think the deeper reason is that it's genuinely shared. Nobody has to buy anything to be there, and you get an eighty-year-old and an eight-year-old using the same path, which feels increasingly rare in a city where so much space is about spending money.

summary.en: Natural and vivid ('a crackly speaker propped against a tree'), with a deeper layer of meaning (shared space without spending); flexible grammar and vocabulary.

samples.text:
I'd like to talk about Green Park, which, to be honest, isn't much to look at: the paint on the benches is peeling and the lake is more of a large pond. But it's about ten minutes' walk from my flat and it's probably my favourite place in the whole city.

What makes it special is the way it works almost like a clock. If you turn up at six in the morning, it's full of retired people doing tai chi so slowly and precisely that it's quite hypnotic to watch. At lunchtime it's office workers perched on walls with their noodles, and by the evening the soundtrack has switched to skateboards, a football being kicked against a fence and someone, there's always someone, practising the saxophone badly under the bridge.

I'm there most evenings, I'd guess five times a week, and I've got my routine down to a fine art: two laps of the pond, then the bench under the big tree, then home.

As for why I keep going back, I think it's that the park asks nothing of you. You don't need a ticket or a reason or any money; you can just exist there for a while. In a city where almost every space is designed to sell you something, that feels less like a luxury and more like a necessity, and I suspect that's why so many different people end up sharing the same few paths.

summary.vi: Kể chuyện tự nhiên, hài hước và giàu hình ảnh; lập luận sâu sắc ('the park asks nothing of you'); ngôn ngữ chính xác tuyệt đối và linh hoạt.
summary.en: Natural, humorous and vivid storytelling; an insightful reason ('the park asks nothing of you'); fully accurate and flexible language.
summary.ja: 自然でユーモアがあり鮮明な語り。洞察ある理由（'the park asks nothing of you'）、完全に正確で柔軟な言語。
